title: WPSS/102/2011 of GIRISH KUMAR Vs GENERAL MANAGER, PUNJAB NATIONAL BANK and ORS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (S/S) No. 102 of 2011
Girish Kumar ...Petitioner

Versus
General Manager,
Punjab National Bank and others ...Respondents
Present:- Mr. S. S. Yadav, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. S. K. Jain, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. B. S.
Thind, Advocate for the respondents.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. The petitioner before this Court was a candidate for
the post of peon which was to be filled up by the Punjab
National Bank through District Employment Officer,
Uttarkashi vide its letter dated 11.10.2010. The
petitioner applied for the said post and he was selected.
However, the appointment has not been given to him, as
consequent to his selection when he presented himself
before the concerned authorities of the respondent Bank
and revealed that he is a graduate, he was informed that
he is not liable to be given appointment as the
qualification given in the advertisement is Intermediate
(i.e. Class XII) and as the petitioner has a qualification
higher than Intermediate, he is not eligible for the said
post. Aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the present writ
petition.
2. A learned Single Judge of this Court has granted
interim order on 3.2.2011 directing the respondent Bank
to keep one post of Peon vacant for the petitioner.
3. Learned Senior Counsel for the respondent Bank
Mr. S. K. Jain has submitted before this Court that the

2
conditions given in the advertisement have to be adhered
to and since there was no maximum or minimum marks
prescribed and only educational qualifications were
prescribed which was Intermediate and since admittedly
the petitioner is a graduate, he made himself ineligible for
the said post. There is another objection raised by the
Senior Counsel for the Bank that in the petitionerís
registration pertaining to the year 2003 as renewed in the
year 2006 and 2009 the qualification of the petitioner
was given as Intermediate. The petitioner has not given
the correct information to the District Employment
Exchange, Uttarkashi otherwise the candidature of the
petitioner was liable to be rejected at the threshold itself
or in the alternative not requisitioned from the
Employment Exchange.
4. The objections raised by the respondent Bank has,
however, no relevance here. Infact the petitioner has been
harassed for irrelevant reasons, which to the say the
least has been unfair.
5. Even if it is assumed for the sake of argument that
the qualification which was required for a candidate was
an Intermediate and once it is advertised as a
qualification the candidate having a graduate degree
would mean that such a person is Intermediate that it is
so is because only after qualifying the Intermediate
examination one is liable to appear for graduation. The
petitioner has Intermediate qualifications and therefore
he was eligible for the said post. To put forward the
argument at this stage that the only qualification was
Intermediate is absolutely irrelevant and the candidature
of the petitioner was wrongly rejected. It is undoubtedly

3
true that even though once selected the candidate does
not get any indefeasible right for having appointed.
However, in the present case, the reasons have been
assigned for not giving appointment to the petitioner are
wholly unreasonable. Holding petitioner ineligible would
be punishing him for being a graduate!
6. As regards the entry in the Employment Exchange
that petitioner is Intermediate, the counsel for the
petitioner contends that entry precedes the period when
petitioner was a graduate or thus he became a graduate
after enrolling himself in the Employment Exchange.
7. In view of the above, the contention of the
respondents is rejected. The writ petition succeeds and is
hereby allowed. A mandamus is issued to the respondent
Bank to give appointment to the petitioner within a
period of one month from the date a certified copy of this
order is produced before concerned authority.
8. No order as to costs.
 (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 14.5.2013
Kuldeep
